question: Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam and Tillana are regular patterns of which of the following classical dance forms of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originating from Tamil Nadu.
 
• The dance form is known for its **fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate footwork combined with expressive hand gestures and facial expressions**.
 
• Regular patterns in Bharatanatyam include **Alarippu, Jatiswaram, Shabdam, Varnam, and Tillana**.
 
• These components form the structure of a traditional Bharatanatyam performance, each with its unique significance and role in storytelling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alarippu** is an invocatory piece that **symbolizes the blossoming of a flower**.
 
• **Jatiswaram** combines intricate footwork with melodic patterns without any expressive elements.
 
• **Shabdam** incorporates expressive gestures and is usually a narrative piece.
 
• **Varnam** is the centerpiece of a **Bharatanatyam recital**, combining both expressive and technical aspects.
 
• **Tillana** is a lively and rhythmic conclusion piece, often highlighting the dancer's technical prowess.
 
• Bharatanatyam is deeply rooted in the spiritual and cultural traditions of India and often depicts themes from Hindu mythology.
